title: Onramp fallthrough matrix + telemetry playpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playpad to capture a compact, runnable onramp experience for new SDK users that emphasizes behavior under partial failures (fallthroughs). Goal: a 10-15 minute hands-on path + an accompanying telemetry/alert matrix that surfaces regressions fast during early adoption and in customer pilots.

Status and audience:
- Draft playground for developer experience + solutions eng to iterate on.
- Primary consumers: SDK docs writers, sample app authors, customer-facing SEs.
- Not final; contains rough TODOs and experiment notes.

High-level constraints:
- Keep the happy path < 15min (including account creation and token copy).
- Surface 3 classes of failure explicitly: network/timeouts, model-variant fallback, and rate-limit/backpressure.
- Provide deterministic synthetic probes so we can surface regressions in telemetry quickly.

Quick 3-step onramp (core flow we want in the quickstart):
1) Key & minimal dependency install (30–90s)
   - npm: npm i @redwood/sdk-lite
   - export REDWOOD_KEY=sk-test-XXXX
   - confirm: redwood health --model gpt-lite-1 --region us-west1

2) Hello-world that streams + fallback (3–6min)
   - A single file that: sends a streaming chat request, logs partial events, then forces a fallback to a smaller quantized variant on simulated OOM.
   - Example psuedo steps:
     - demo_chat.js: create client -> start streaming -> print tokens -> after 2s inject simulated error (simulate with env REDWOOD_SIM_FAIL=oom) -> verify fallback to gpt-lite-1-q4

3) Local probe & telemetry check (2–5min)
   - Run `npm run sdk-probe` which emits a deterministic vector of requests (prefixes, short/long sequences, embedding call).
   - Telemetry dashboard should show: probe success rate, 95p latency for tokens, fallthrough_count, cache_hit_rate.

Playpad: fallthrough matrix (decision table)
- Columns: Trigger, Primary action, Fallback action, User-visible signal, Telemetry key to monitor
- Rows (examples):
  - network timeout 500ms: retry once (exp backoff), then route to region fallback; signal: request_timed_out; key: onramp.probe.timeout_count
  - kernel OOM on large model: immediately restart with quantized variant; signal: model.oom.fallback; key: onramp.probe.model_fallback_count
  - rate-limit 429: if customer tier == free -> degrade to short-completion mode (truncate max_tokens to 64) and flag quota_exhausted; key: onramp.probe.rate_limit_count
  - cache-miss spike: fallthrough to cold-path, emit synthetic cache_age metric; key: onramp.probe.cache_miss_spike

Telemetry playbook (what to show in the quickstart dashboard)
- Minimum tiles for the first-run dashboard:
  1) Probe success rate (past 10m) -> target 99%
  2) 95p generation latency (tokens/sec) -> target baseline +- 20%
  3) Fallthrough events (by type): model_fallback_count, region_failover_count, retry_count
  4) Cost estimate meter for probe (tokens used / $ est)
  5) Top failing probe traces (sample ids) with prompt and partial outputs

Instrumentation guidance for the SDK (what to emit)
- Emit lightweight envelope per request: {probe_id, step, user_tier, model, seq_len, was_fallback, latency_ms, status_code} (we'll record as discrete telemetry keys).
- Minimal event list (names): onramp.probe.start, onramp.probe.step.partial_token, onramp.probe.complete, onramp.probe.fallback, onramp.probe.error
- Attach tags: environment:dev|prod, region, sample_app_version

Synthetic probe recipes (for CI and SE demos)
- quick-probe-short: 5 requests, short sequences (8–32 tokens), 10s between requests (simulates interactive web).
- quick-probe-long: 3 requests, long sequences (512 tokens), 30s between requests (simulates doc-gen).
- embed-smoke: 10 embedding calls with random but fixed seed vectors for deterministic output hash check.
- failure-harness: inject network errors (env REDWOOD_SIM_NET=drop25 -> drops 25% requests) and assert fallback_count > 0 in telemetry within 2m.

Local quickstart sample layout (single-file champion)
- File: onramp-demo.js (single file with tiny helper functions)
- contains: setup(), runStreamingChat(), runEmbedding(), runProbeSuite()
- helpful CLI: `node onramp-demo.js --probe quick-probe-short`

User-visible UX copy (minimal, for the quickstart page)
- Headline: "Get a streaming chat up in 10 minutes — with graceful fallbacks"
- Subheadline: "Run the demo, watch a live probe, and inspect the fallback events that protect your app from outages."
- Callouts: "Try the 'failure-harness' to see fallbacks in action — safe, local-only simulation."

Failure modes we should explicitly demo (and why)
- OOM fallback: demonstrates quantized variant + minimal quality regression and cost reduction; important because many customers worry about large model memory cliffs.
- Region failover: shows multi-region routing working and how latency SLOs are preserved.
- Rate-limited degrade: shows UX-first degrade (shorter completions) instead of hard errors.

Acceptance criteria for the quickstart (what we ship as "done")
- Playbook file + single-file demo runs in <15min from blank macOS/linux dev box.
- `sdk-probe` emits telemetry keys visible in the console dashboard within 60s.
- README contains explicit steps to reproduce three failure demos.
- One SE runbook (2 pages) with troubleshooting checklist for the three failure modes.

Open questions / TODOs
- QA: who owns the deterministic probe harness (eng-serving-runtime vs eng-devexp)? (TODO: ask in #devexp-ops)
- Should fallbacks be opt-in via config (allow customer to disable auto-fallbacks)? trade-offs: transparency vs OOM protection.
- How conservative should the default retry/backoff policy be for the quickstart? (TODO: propose defaults and A/B test)
- Telemetry: confirm retention / PII scrub rules for sample prompts in traces.

Immediate next steps (short checklist)
- [ ] Drop single-file demo into repo under examples/onramp-demo (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Add `sdk-probe` npm script + simple JSON reporter (owner: Alex)
- [ ] Wire minimal dashboard tile templates and verify with local probe (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Create a short SE one-pager and run 2 SE show-and-tells next sprint (owner: Samir)

Notes to self (random scribbles)
- Keep the demo deterministic — use fixed seeds for embeddings.
- Consider a `--visualize` flag that prints a tiny ascii timeline of partial tokens and fallback transitions.
- If time: add a minimal ReDoc or HTML page that loads the tiny telemetry JSON to show real-time tile updates (helpful for demos without full console access).

Slack/links to mention in the doc:
- #devexp-onramp (draft), #solutions-se (for pilot feedback), ENG-2148 (probe harness ticket).

End of playpad.

(If you pick this up: please append new experimental notes under a date header, e.g., "2025-01-15 — added failure-harness recipe; 2025-01-22 — adjusted probe target latency to 95p <= 350ms")
